main_body: Two half-timbered gabled house fronts joined by a narrow connecting wall, each with a large tiled roof, a plaster and timber front, windows with flower boxes, and a door on the left house
top_band: Orange/gold roof tiles (L~130-216) from about row 5 to row 64, a large foreshortened slope clearly lighter and different in tone and texture from the pale plaster wall below
evidence: The roof reads as a tiled slope seen from above, ending in a dark timber eave line with a shadow row over the gable triangle and walls. Below it is the plaster and timber south face, with timber framing, inset windows with sills, and a door. It is built the same way as the Beodeul house references (roof slope above a front wall). The roof is clearly a surface, not a rim, and no receding isometric side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights across about 5-6 steps (gold, orange, mid, dark red-brown, plum). The plaster has speckle dots and the timber has dark brown tinted outlines. Measured facts match the references: median 11 colours per tile (references 18 and 11), 195 distinct colours (references 185 and 66), 0% flat-fill coverage, and only 5% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted. It would sit next to the references without looking thinner or more sticker-like.
